## Solution

The surface $S$ is the paraboloid $z = 1 - x^2 - y^2$ for $z \ge 0$ (i.e., $x^2+y^2 \le 1$), with boundary curve $C$ given by $x^2+y^2=1,\ z=0$.

By **Stokes' theorem**:
$$\iint_S (\nabla\times\vec F)\cdot\hat n\,dS = \oint_C \vec F\cdot d\vec r.$$

On $C$ we have $z=0$, so $e^z=1$ and $z=0$, giving
$$\vec F = (x+2y)\,\mathbf i + (y+x^2)\,\mathbf j + 0\,\mathbf k.$$

Parameterize $C$ (counterclockwise, matching the upward normal of $S$):
$$x=\cos t,\quad y=\sin t,\quad z=0,\quad 0\le t\le 2\pi.$$
$$dx=-\sin t\,dt,\quad dy=\cos t\,dt.$$

Then
$$\vec F\cdot d\vec r = (x+2y)\,dx + (y+x^2)\,dy$$
$$= (\cos t+2\sin t)(-\sin t)\,dt + (\sin t+\cos^2 t)(\cos t)\,dt$$
$$= -\cos t\sin t - 2\sin^2 t + \sin t\cos t + \cos^3 t$$
$$= -2\sin^2 t + \cos^3 t.$$

Integrating over $[0,2\pi]$:
$$\int_0^{2\pi} -2\sin^2 t\,dt = -2\cdot\pi = -2\pi,$$
$$\int_0^{2\pi}\cos^3 t\,dt = 0 \quad\text{(odd harmonic)}.$$

Therefore
$$\iint_S (\nabla\times\vec F)\cdot\hat n\,dS = -2\pi,$$
and
$$\left|\iint_S (\nabla\times\vec F)\cdot\hat n\,dS\right| = 2\pi = \alpha\pi.$$

Hence $\boxed{\alpha = 2}$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
